issues.description: The problem statement requires constructors to accept attributes in the same order as shown in the UML (top-to-bottom). The UML for ExcellenceLand lists attributes in the order: excellencyLevel (double), excellentEnough (boolean). The problem tasks also add a private List<Ride> rides attribute but do not specify its position in the constructor parameter order. The solution implementation defines the ExcellenceLand constructor as (List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel), which does not follow the UML attribute order and is ambiguous relative to the task description. This mismatch between the UML/instruction and the solution/template can confuse students about the required constructor parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order unambiguous and consistent with the UML/instructions. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to show the rides attribute and its intended position (for example, list rides as the first attribute in the UML if the constructor should accept it first), or (B) change the ExcellenceLand constructor to follow the UML attribute order and then append the rides parameter (e.g. public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides)) and update the solution and any tests accordingly.
